answer: Each agent's identity is bound to a costly, non-transferable footprint: an escrow that unlocks only after it serves as a trellis for newcomers, co-signing their earliest settlements. Those endorsements accumulate into a living reef of interlocking obligations, so a swarm of clones cannot bootstrap; forged identities have no settled history to anchor to, and the shared atlas of provenance discounts every claim by the sunk cost behind it.
